description:
Dependency-graph queries run on one traversal primitive, one cycle detector and one reverse-dependency index, so they stay linear in graph size as the repository grows. The cycle detector also reports which issues form a cycle.

## Background

**Traversals.** Eight separate stack or queue walks cover the same dependency relation. Six are in `crates/jit/src/graph/mod.rs`: `traverse` (`:132`), `is_reachable` (`:235`), `get_transitive_dependents` (`:278`), `get_transitive_dependencies` (`:309`), `has_path_excluding_direct` (`:403`) and `find_shortest_path` (`:468`). The other two are `graph/hierarchy.rs:716` `dependency_closure` and `domain/queries.rs:443` `bracket_scope_ids`. `is_transitive` (`:397`) and `has_path_excluding_direct` have only test callers. `HierarchyNode` re-declares `GraphNode`'s id and dependencies, which forces the `EdgeView` adapter in `transitively_reduced_edges` (`hierarchy.rs:484-509`). `bracket_scope_ids` runs a linear `find` per visited node and a linear `any` per edge, which is $O(V^2 d)$. It runs on scoped validation and gate scope checks.

**Cycle detection.** Two detectors exist. `validate_dag` (`graph/mod.rs:352`) recurses through `has_cycle_dfs` (`:368`) with two `HashSet<String>` sets. Its recursion depth equals the chain length, and it returns a bare `GraphError::CycleDetected` with no path. `graph/keyed.rs:33` `find_keyed_cycle` is iterative and returns the cycle path. Batch create, breakdown, template expansion and the profile graph use it. `batch_create::detect_cycle` (`batch_create.rs:640`) is a thin wrapper whose four unit tests repeat the `keyed.rs` matrix.

**Reverse dependencies.** `get_dependents` (`graph/mod.rs:269`) scans every node and allocates a `String` per node per call. `get_transitive_dependents` calls it once per visited node, which is $O(V(V+E))$. `get_isolated_nodes` (`:337`) calls it once per node on every `validate_repository`. The private `neighbors(Direction::Dependents)` (`:90`) already builds the reverse index in one pass, but only `traverse` and `expand` use it. The graph rule evaluator scans all issues per visited node in `children_of` (`validation/graph.rs:1169-1174`) and per firing issue in `linked_issues` (`:1339-1348`). Issue deletion rebuilds a position scan and the whole issue map once per dependent (`commands/issue.rs:86-97`), which is $O(D \cdot N)$.

**Transitive reduction.** `compute_transitive_reduction` (`graph/mod.rs:435`) runs a fresh `is_reachable` DFS from each of a node's other dependencies for every dependency. That is $O(d^2)$ traversals per node. `find_redundant_edges` (`:512`) repeats it for every node. `jit dep add` clones every issue into a candidate set and runs the whole-graph check (`commands/dependency.rs:702-704`), and the batch reject path does it again per edge on a fresh clone (`:819-820`). `resolve_hierarchy` runs the same reduction through `transitively_reduced_edges` on every server `GET /graph`, on graph tree and export, and in the artifact inventory. `find_shortest_path` clones the whole path for every enqueued edge. The transitive depends-on rule runs one such BFS per (source, target) pair (`validation/graph.rs:1459`), which is $O(S \cdot T \cdot (V+E))$. At 1,170 issues none of this shows in profiles, so these are scaling gaps.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The graph module exposes one traversal primitive, parameterised by direction, depth bound and stop predicate. Reachability, transitive dependencies and dependents, shortest path, hierarchy closure and bracket scope derive from it, and no other walk over dependency edges remains in `crates/jit/src`.
- [hard] REQ-02: `is_transitive` and `has_path_excluding_direct` are removed. Hierarchy nodes are graph nodes with only a type name added, and the `EdgeView` adapter is removed.
- [hard] REQ-03: Exactly one cycle detector exists, and it is iterative. DAG validation, dependency addition, batch create, template expansion and profile graph resolution all call it. `has_cycle_dfs` and the `batch_create::detect_cycle` wrapper are removed.
- [hard] REQ-04: A cycle error carries the cycle's issue path, and `jit validate` and `jit dep add` report the issues that form the cycle.
- [hard] REQ-05: Cycle detection and DAG validation succeed on a 100,000-issue dependency chain without stack overflow.
- [hard] REQ-06: Each graph builds its reverse-dependency index once. Direct dependents, transitive dependents and isolated nodes read that index, and isolated-node detection is $O(V+E)$.
- [hard] REQ-07: Graph rule evaluation, scoped-bracket resolution and issue deletion resolve neighbours through id and reverse-dependency indexes. None scans the full issue list per visited node or per dependent.
- [hard] REQ-08: The transitive depends-on rule computes one dependency closure per source and tests every target against it. Shortest-path search builds its result path once, from a predecessor map.
- [hard] REQ-09: Transitive reduction finds each node's redundant direct dependencies with work $O(V+E)$ per node, sharing one visited set across that node's dependencies. Per-node reduction and whole-graph redundant-edge detection derive from that one function.
- [hard] REQ-10: Adding a dependency checks only the edges the new edge can make redundant, with no clone of the full issue set. The batch path does not rebuild the graph per edge.
- [hard] REQ-11: Property-based tests over generated graphs prove each property once at the graph layer. Traversal matches a reference closure in both directions. The cycle detector reports a cycle exactly when one exists, and the reported path is a cycle in the graph. Reduction preserves reachability and leaves no redundant edge. The reverse index equals the inverted adjacency.
- [hard] REQ-12: Consumers of the cycle detector and the traversal test only their wiring. Tests outside the graph module that repeat its cycle-detection matrix are removed.

## Notes

- Serves @/charter/D-18 (one mechanism in place of several) and @/charter/D-20 (one computation per capability).
- Invariants: @/inv/dag-acyclic, @/inv/convention-convergence, @/inv/orthogonal-tests, @/inv/architecture-dependency-direction.
- Graph operations require proptest coverage under the repository's testing rules.
title: Run graph queries on one traversal, one cycle detector and one reverse index
